moqt.note: Every SDK implements draft-ietf-moq-transport-20 and no other version. protocolId is that draft's wire identifier (draft §1.4 rule: "moqt-" plus the draft number), offered as the WebTransport protocol identifier (WT-Available-Protocols / ALPN).

authentication.note: An explicit jwt parameter already present on the URL takes precedence over a token callback. An empty jwt parameter is rejected as an argument error, not treated as absent.

limits.note: moq-relay implementation limits, not draft-20 ones. maxObjectPropertiesBytes is the limit on an object's encoded property block (MAX_OBJECT_EXTENSIONS since 0.17.0): the relay stops the subgroup stream on a larger block and the object is lost with no error to the subscriber, so both SDKs refuse such a write as an argument error. limits.maxObjectPropertiesBytes stays the core's draft-20 bound for what a subscriber decodes. maxTrackProperties is the number of track properties the relay parses from SUBSCRIBE_OK (MAX_PROPERTIES in 0.17.0): past it, the relay refuses every subscriber with REQUEST_ERROR 18 'too many' and the publisher hears nothing, so both SDKs refuse such a track at registration.

maxTrackPropertiesBytes is the encoded track property block a publisher's SUBSCRIBE_OK can carry: the 16-bit control message length (65535) less the track alias, a varint of up to 9 bytes that is the peer's request ID and so unknown at registration, and the 1-byte count of the message parameters, of which the SDKs send none. Both SDKs refuse a larger block at registration; the core holds the bound.

trackProperties.note: Track property values draft-20 restricts (sections 12.4 and 12.5): a Default Publisher Priority above 255 is invalid and a Default Publisher Group Order other than 1 (ascending) or 2 (descending) is a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION. moq-relay refuses every subscriber to such a track with REQUEST_ERROR 18 'invalid value', so both SDKs refuse it at registration.
